```text
Washington, Tuesday, February 21, 1950
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10110
P resid en t’s C o m m unications P olicy
B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in
me as President of the United States,
it is hereby ordered as follows :
1. There is hereby created a board to
be known as the President’ s Communi­
cations Policy Board which shall be com­
posed of a chairman and four other
members to be designated by the Presi­
dent.
2. It shall be the function of the Board
to study the present and potential use
of radio and wire communications facili­
ties by governmental and non-govern­
mental agencies and to make and present
to the President evaluations and recom­
mendations in the national interest con­
cerning (a) policies for the most effective
use of radio frequencies by governmental
and non-governmental users and alter­
native administrative arrangements in
the Federal Government for the sound
effectuation of such policies, (b) policies
with respect to international radio and
wire communications, (c) the relation­
ship of Government communications to
non-government communications, and
(d) such related policy matters as the
Board may determine.
3. The Board is authorized to hear and
consult with representatives of industry
and the Federal Government concerned
with the subjects under study by the
Board. All executive departments and
agencies of the Federal Government are
authorized and directed to cooperate with
the Board in its work and to furnish the
Board such information as it may re­
quire in the performance of its duties.
The Board shall protect the security of
any classified information submitted to
it.
4. Each member of the Board shall,
while away from his home or regular
place of business and engaged in the
official business of the Board, receive
actual traveling expenses and per diem
allowances in lieu of subsistence in ac­
cordance with rates established by the
Standardized Government Travel Reg­
ulations, as amended.
5. During the fiscal year 1950 the ex­
penditures of the Board and the travel-
ing expenses and per diem allowances
of the members thereof shall be paid out
of an allotment made by the President
from the appropriation appearing under
the heading “Emergency Fund for the
President” in the Independent Offices
Appropriation Act, 1950 (Public Law 266,
approved August 24, 1949); and during
the fiscal year 1951 the same shall be
similarly paid from any corresponding
or like appropriation made available for
the fiscal year 1951. Such payments
shall be made without regard to the
provisions of (a) section 3681 of the Re­
vised Statutes (31 U. S. C. 672), (b) sec­
tion 9 of the act of March 4, 1909, 35
Stat. 1027 (31 U. S. C. 673), and (c)
such other laws as the President may
hereafter specify.
The Board shall terminate one year
after the date of this order.
H arry  S. T ruman
T h e W h it e H o use,
February 17,1950.
[F. R. Doc. 50-1503; Filed, Feb. 17, 1950;
3:57 p. m.]
```

```text
THE PRESIDENT 46293
Executive Order 11882 October 6, 1975
Membership of Energy Research and Development Administration on
Established River Basin Commissions
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 202 of the Water
Resources Planning Act (79 Stat. 247, 42 U.S.C. 1962b— 1), and as
President of the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Section 3(2)  of Executive Order No. 11345 of April 20,
1967, as amended, establishing the Great Lakes Basin Commission, is
amended by adding “ Energy Research and Development Administra­
tion,” immediately after “ Department of Transportation.”
Sec. 2. Section 3(2)  of each of the following Executive orders is
amended by deleting “ Atomic Energy Commission”  and substituting
therefor “ Energy Research and Development Administration” :
(a ) Executive Order No. 11371 of September 6, 1967, as amended,
establishing the New England River Basins Commission;
(b ) Executive Order No. 11578 of January 13, 1971, establishing
the Ohio River Basin Commission;
(c) Executive Order No. 11658 of March 22, 1972, establishing the
Missouri River Basin Commission; and
(d ) Executive Order No. 11659 of March 22, 1972, as amended,
establishing the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission-.
Sec. 3. The Administrator of the Energy Research and Development
Administration shall appoint a member to each river basin commission
to serve as the representative of that agency as soon as practicable after
the date of issuance of this order. -
T h e W hite H o use,
October 6,1975.
{FR Doc.75-27129 Filed 10-6-75;! 1:22 a.m.]
FEDERAL REGISTER, V O L 40, NO, 195— TUESDAY, OCTOBER 7, 1975
```

```text
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Act of this date, entitled "An Act to authorize the President to extend enlistments in the Armed Forces of the United States," and as President of the United States and Commander in Chief of the armed forces of the United States, I hereby extend for a period of twelve months all enlistments in the Army, the United States Navy, and the United States Marine Corps, including the Naval Reserve and the Marine Corps Reserve, and in any component of the Air Force of the United States, which shall expire at any time after the date of this order and prior to July 9, 1951: Provided, That nothing contained herein shall be construed to prevent voluntary re-enlistments or voluntary extension of existing enlistments under provisions of applicable laws or the regulations of the Departments of the Army, Navy and Air Force.
```

```text
SYSTEM
[23,789]
PART 555— BOARD RULINGS
Title Evidence
F e br uar y 5, 1970.
Resolved that the Federal Home Loan
Bank Board, for the purpose of permit­
ting Federal savings and loan associa­
tions to make loans insured by the
Federal Housing Administration on the
security of real estate sold by the Depart­
ment of Housing and Urban Develop­
ment without obtaining new title evi­
dence of first liens, hereby amends Part
555 of the rules and regulations for the
Federal Savings and Loan System (12
CFR Part 555) by adding a new § 555.13
to read as follows:
§ 555.13 First liens on the security of
properties sold by the Secretary of
HUD.
Section 5(c) of the Home Owners’
Loan Act of 1933, as amended, provides
that Federal savings and loan associa­
tions may make mortgage loans insured
by the Federal Housing Administration
and secured by first liens on improved
real estate. The Secretary of HUD, when
disposing of properties which are ac­
quired by lien under the default provi­
sions of an earlier insured loan, may sell
said properties to individuals and insure
new loans to finance these purchases. In
addition, the Department of HUD, upon
the recommendation of the General Ac­
counting Office, has provided, as set forth
in §§ 230.390 and 230.402 of FHA regula­
tions (24 CFR 230.390 and 230.402), the
procedure whereby such mortgage loans
may be insured without documentary
evidence establishing the quality and
validity of the mortgagee’s lien. Since the
FHA procedure offers protection to Fed­
eral associations tantamount to that of a
first lien, such loans shall be considered
to be secured by a first lien for purposes
of the rules and regulations for the Fed­
eral Savings and Loan System, even
though new title evidence has not been
obtained.
(Sec. 5, 48 Stat. 132, as amended; 12 U.S.C.
1464. Reorg. Plan No. 3 of 1947, 12 F.R. 4981,
3 CFR, 1943-48 Comp., p. 1071)
By the Federal Home Loan Bank
Board.

Assistant Secretary.
```

```text
Title 3—The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11579
Overseas Private Investment Corporation
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Foreign Assistance Act
of 1961 (75 Stat. 424), as amended (hereinafter the “Act” ), and
section 301 of title 3 of the United States Code, and as President of
the United States, it is ordered as follows :
S e c t io n 1. Transfer to Overseas Private Investment Corporation.  All
obligations, assets and related rights and responsibilities arising out of,
or related to, predecessor programs and authorities similar to those
provided for in sections 234(a), (b) and (d) of the Act are hereby
transferred to the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (herein­
after the “Corporation” ).
S e c. 2. Delegation of functions, (a) The functions conferred upon the
President by sections 621(b), 625(d) (1), 627, 628, 629(b), 630, and
635 (d) of the Act insofar as such functions relate to the operation of
the Corporation, its activities, or personnel are 'hereby delegated to the
Corporation : Provided, That the concurrence of the Secretary of State
shall be required with respect to the exercise by the Corporation of so
much of the functions herein delegated pursuant to section 625(d) (1)
of the Act as consists of authorization of compensation at any of the
rates provided for the Foreign Service Reserve and Staff by the Foreign
Service Act of 1946 for persons employed or assigned by the Corporation.
(b) The function of prescribing regulations relating to the reinstate­
ment or restoration of officers and employees of the Corporation to
other government positions, when their appointment to a position in
the Corporation was made from another government position and their
separation from the Corporation was not made for cause, is hereby dele­
gated to the Civil Service Commission. _
S e c. 3. Allocation and transfer of funds.  Funds made available under
section 232 of the Act (repealed by section 105 of the Foreign Assistance
Act of 1969) which are obligated but unexpended are hereby trans­
ferred to the Corporation.
Sec. 4. General provisions, (a) As used in this order, the words
“function” or “functions” include any duty, obligation, power, author­
ity, responsibility, right, privilege, discretion, or activity.
(b) The Corporation shall be deemed to be the successor of the
Agency for International Development and the Administrator thereof,
with respect to all functions vested in the Corporation pursuant to law.
„(c) Except to the extent that they may be inconsistent with this
order, all determinations, authorizations, regulations, rulings, certificates,
```

```text
Army pursuant to the act of May 16,
1946, c. 261, 60 Stat. 182, as amended by
the act of August 5,1947, c. 497, 61 Stat.
779, together with (a) such supplies,,
equipment, temporary structures, utili­
ties and facilities pertaining thereto as
are located therein or are in depots or
other places under the jurisdiction of
the American Graves Registration Serv­
ice which are in excess of the needs of
the Department of the Army and are
requested by the American Battle Mon­
uments Commission, and (b) the cem­
etery records currently maintained for
the operation of such cemeteries, includ­
ing records pertinent to the acquisition
of real estate upon which the cemeteries
and their appurtenances are situated,
are hereby transferred to the American
Battle Monuments Commission; such
transfer to become effective as to any
particular cemetery or group of cem­
eteries upon the completion of the oper­
ational mission of the Department of
the Army with respect to such cemetery
or group of cemeteries, but in no in­
stance later than December 31, 1951, or
at such earlier date as may be deter­
mined by the President or the Congress
pursuant to the said act of May 16,1946,
as amended by the act of August 5,1947.
2. The Department of the Army shall
have the right to re-enter any of such
cemeteries subsequent to the effective
date of the transfer of functions with
respect thereto for the purpose of mak­
ing exhumations or reinterments should
any such action become necessary.
3. There shall be transferred to the
American Battle Monuments Commis­
sion so much of the unexpended balances
of appropriations now, or which may be­
come, available to the Department of the
Army for the performance of the func­
tions transferred by the provisions of this
order as the Director of the Bureau of
the Budget may deem necessary for use
prior to July 1, 1949, in connection with
such functions.
Harry S. T ruman
T he W hite H ouse ,
```

```text
Reorganization Plan No. 6
of 1961
Prepared by the President and trans­
mitted to the Senate and the House of

visions of the Reorganization Act of

Federal H ome L oan B ank B oard
Section  1 . Transfer of ' functions.
Subject to the provisions of section 2(a)
of this reorganization plan, and to the
extent not vested in the Chairman of the
Federal Home Loan Bank Board (here­
inafter referred to as the Chairman) in
the absence of this reorganization plan,
the executive and administrative func­
tions of the Federal Home Loan Bank
Board (hereinafter referred to as the
B o ard ), including the following-de­
scribed functions of the Board, are
hereby transferred from the Board to
the Chairman:
(1 ) ^The appointment and removal of
personnel employed under the Board.
(2) The distribution of business among
such personnel and among administra­
tive units of the Board.
(3) The direction of personnel who
perform, or who supervise the perform­
ance of, any function of the Board or of
the Chairman or of any agency under
the Board.
(4) The communication to personnel
employed under the Board of applicable
Board policies to be followed by such
personnel in the performance of their
work and the subsequent enforcement of
such policies.
(5) The over-all management, func­
tioning and organization of the Board,
including (a ) the formulation and im­
plementation of plans and policies de­
signed to increase the effectiveness of
the Board in the administration of the
laws it is charged with administering and
the initiation of ways and means of cor­
recting or preventing avoidable delays
in the performance of any work or the

entation to the Bureau of the Budget of

authorizations for the Board and the

( 8) The calling of the Board into spe­
cial session whenever any matter or busi­
ness of the Board so requires, but in any
event for the consideration of any mat­
ter or business upon request of one or
both of the other members of the Board.
Sec. 2. Performance of transferred
functions,  (a ) (1) In carrying out any
of his functions under the provisions of
section 1  hereof the Chairman shall be
governed by general policies of the
Board and by such regulatory decisions,
findings, and determinations as the
Board may by law be authorized to
make.
(2) The appointment by the Chair­
man of the heads of major administra­
tive units under the Board shall be sub­
ject to the approval of the Board.
(3) Personnel employed regularly and
full time in the immediate offices of
Board members other than the Chair­
man shall not be affected by the provi­
sions of this reorganization plan.
(b) The Chairman may from time to
time make such provisions as he shall
deem appropriate authorizing the per­
formance by any officer, employee, or ad­
ministrative unit under his jurisdiction
of any function transferred to the
Chairman by the provisions of section 1
of this reorganization plan or of any
function vested in the Chairman in con­
sequence of his status as the chief ex­
ecutive officer of the Board.
```

```text
Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11468
AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 11248, PLACING CERTAIN POSI­
TIONS IN LEVELS IV AND V OF THE FEDERAL EXECUTIVE SALARY
SCHEDULE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 5317 of title 5
of the United States Code, as amended, Executive Order No. 11248 ^of
October 10,1965, as amended, is further amended as follows:
1. Section 1 of that Order, placing certain positions in level IV  of
the Federal Executive Salary Schedule, is amended by deleting “(9)
Executive Director,* Cabinet Committee on Price Stability”, and in­
serting in lieu thereof “ (9) Deputy Under Secretary for International
Labor Affairs, Department of Labor”.
2. Section 2 of that Order, placing certain positions in level V of the
Federal Executive Salary Schedule, is amended by adding thereto the
following:
(23) Deputy Assistant Postmaster General, Bureau of Operations,
Post Office Department.
(24) Director, Office of Minority Business Enterprise, Department
of Commerce.
T h e W h it e H ouse ,
May 10,1969.
[F.R. Doc. 69-5781; Filed, May 12, 1969; 1: 22 p.m.]
```

- **ACT:EO:10057>EO:10087@0969bf2ea027b1a2**; Sedd879ac3cf322d7a7fc9a62; {"actor_id":"EO:10087","char_end":200,"char_start":0,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2390,"char_start":1092,"text":"McKinley, Philippine Islands, now vested in or exercised by the Secretary of the Army pursuant to the act of May 16, 1946, c. 261, 60 Stat. 182, as amended by the act of August 5, 1947, c. 497, 61 Stat. 779, together with (a) such supplies, equipment, temporary structures, utilities and facilities pertaining thereto as are located therein or are in depots or other places overseas under the jurisdiction of the American Graves Registration Service and are determined by the American Battle Monuments Commission to be required for the discharge of its responsibilities under this order, and (b) the cemetery records currently maintained for the operation of such cemeteries, including records pertinent to the acquisition of real estate upon which the cemeteries and their appurtenances are situated, are hereby transferred to the American Battle Monuments Commission; such transfer to become effective as to any particular cemetery or group of cemeteries upon the completion of the operational mission of the Department of the Army with respect to such cemetery or group of cemeteries, but in no instance later than December 31, 1951, or at such earlier date as may be determined by the President or the Congress pursuant to the said act of May 16, 1946, as amended by the act of August 5, 1947.\""}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10057>EO:10087@0969bf2ea027b1a2","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. reserved the Army's right to re-enter the cemeteries for exhumations or reinterments after the transfer (paragraph 2); and provided a transfer of unexpended Army appropriation balances for use before a stated date (paragraph 3). I read the held Federal Register text layer (verified whole-order span) and the dossier inventory of three numbered paragraphs is complete. EO 10087 of December 3, 1949 (14 FR 7287, held Federal Register text) amended paragraphs 1 and 3 to read as set out; this is a strike-and-insert style rewrite, so paragraphs 1 and 3 continue as amended and EO 10087 is recorded as a later event with before and after text, not an end. Ends: paragraph 3 is a time-limited authority for the Director of the Bureau of the Budget; its own terms confine transfers to use before July 1, 1949 (original) and, after EO 10087, before July 1, 1950, so it is terminated by its own terms (recorded inclusive, 1949-06-30 for the original window; the exclusive reading is the start of July 1, 1949); EO 10087 re-set the window on December 3, 1949, after the first window had closed, and the second window closed on 1950-06-30 inclusive. No source held shows whether any balances were transferred, so no performance date is claimed. Paragraphs 1 and 2 have no end date or condition other than the paragraph 1 transfer timetable. Paragraph 1 is a performed, self-executing transfer whose per-cemetery effective dates are not held; its outer bound is 1951-12-31 and the allocation of administration to the Commission persists. Current predicate: the U.S. Code in force (36 U.S.C. 2111(b)(1)(A), held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t36-s2111.txt, and the same section's notes, which set out EO 10057 as amended by EO 10087 as provided) refers to the duties and powers transferred to the Commission by EO 10057 as amended by EO 10087 and does not repeal them; the lookup shows the Code's four hits on this order, and the OFR-catalog search reports only EO 10087 and a mis-citation. The held Federal Register texts of EO 10087 and 10088 cite this order (10088 only prints on the same page). I found no revocation or supersession in the held orders. Route: original_plus_bounded_search with the amendment attached; the Code text is a continuation lead read by me, not a packet evidence record. Limit: the Code edition stops at 2026-10-09 and the held texts are Federal Register text layers. Nothing here is a certification.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"The only own-terms ends are paragraph 3's use windows (before July 1, 1949, re-set by EO 10087 to before July 1, 1950) and the paragraph 1 outer date of December 31, 1951 for the transfers to take effect, which is a deadline for performance and not an end of the Commission's functions. EO 10087 amends and does not revoke; no other held order names EO 10057 (searched held texts: EO 10087, EO 10088 which only shares a page, the 1989 OFR snapshot and the Code). An earlier revocation or supersession is not shown.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Paragraph 2 depends on paragraph 1 only for the effective date of each transfer and is separately a standing Army right; it does not end with the paragraph 3 fund authority. Paragraph 1's supplies and records transfers are part of the same transfer command. The fund transfer in paragraph 3 is independent and time-limited.\",\"savings_check\":\"No savings clause in the order; the savings description above records the accrued and transferred consequences and their sources. I read the held Federal Register text layer (verified whole-order span 1214 to 3732). The dossier inventory was a single sole-paragraph clause; I replaced it with four section clauses (lead and section 1 together, section 2, section 3, section 4) at absolute character offsets of the held text so each section has its own state. Later events (both held as Federal Register texts): EO 10649 of Dec. 28, 1955 (20 FR 10095), effective January 1, 1956 under its paragraph 2, rewrote sections 1 and 2 (section 1 for travel from home to first duty station, section 2 for travel from last duty station to home, without regard to actual performance); EO 12683 of July 21, 1989 (54 FR 31162) rewrote section 1 into a single rule tied to allowable travel time and Secretaries' regulations, deleted section 2 and renumbered sections 3 and 4 as sections 2 and 3. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the rewrites of section 1 are amendments (recorded as later events with before and after text) and the clause continues; the deletion of section 2 is an express ending, dated July 21, 1989 (no delayed effective date appears in EO 12683; it was published July 26, 1989). Section 4 is an effective-date clause spent when the order took effect on 1950-09-01. Searches: number search of the held Federal Register order texts and the lookup show only EO 10649, EO 12683 and the 1989 OFR snapshot naming this order; the three bounded machine searches have 0 U.S. Code hits, 0 eCFR hits and 2 OFR-catalog hits (the two amendments). Route: original_plus_bounded_search, with both amendments attached. Limits: no current text of 37 U.S.C. 204(b) (cited by EO 12683 as authority) is held and the Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere, so continuation rests on the absence of any held ending and on EO 12683 re-basing the authority in 1989; displacement by a later statute or unnumbered action cannot be excluded. The texts are Federal Register text layers, not page-checked images. govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, signed March 8, 1951. Inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses: 1, transferring the civil-defense part of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, to remain under the Administrator's jurisdiction until further order of the President; 2, transferring related property, records and personnel; 3, effective as of March 4, 1951. Ending: section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 (59 FR 29525, held government printing) provides that Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247) is superseded or revoked; the U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note says the same and gives the date June 3, 1994. Section 904 has no stated effective date, so the end is read as effective on signing, 1994-06-03. Unnamed earlier candidates, disclosed under the unnamed-instruments ruling of 2026-10-21 (they do not name Executive Order 10222 and are not ends): Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 (the editorial note in the held OFR 1989 Codification says it terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration effective 1958-07-01 and consolidated its functions into the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization) and Executive Order 10952 of 1961-07-20 (the same note says civil defense functions were later transferred to the Secretary of Defense). The same 1989 Codification still prints Executive Order 10222 as in force on 1989-01-20, after both events. The plan's own text and Executive Order 10952 do not appear in the held corpus as acting on this order. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958, which terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration, and Executive Order 10952 of 1961, which moved civil defense functions to the Secretary of Defense: neither names Executive Order 10222 in any held text, and no held source shows the order's commands extinguished by them; the 1989 Codification still printed the order as in force. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments, a statute or order that does not name the target does not end it; the end is the instrument that names it. They are disclosed as unnamed earlier candidates. (2) The phrase until further order of the President in clause 1 is an own-terms contingent end; the only held presidential order ending it is Executive Order 12919. (3) The one-time transfers in clause 2 were presumably carried out in 1951 but no held source dates their performance, so no exhaustion date is asserted and the express supersession is the first held end. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Independent commands: clause 1 (jurisdiction of the transferred functions under the Administrator until further order of the President) and clause 2 (transfer of property, records and personnel) are distinct commands of the same order; clause 3 fixes the effective date. None is shown in held evidence to have a separate source, statute or earlier sunset; each shares the express supersession by Executive Order 12919, with the executed transfers saved as accrued effects.\",\"savings_check\":\"Savings and residual effects: accrued effects of executed transfers (state transferred_or_accrued) with the Executive Order 12919 section 903 saving language as source.\",\"scope_check\":\"Scope: section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 names Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247) without exception, so it reaches all three clauses. The dossier note that the 1989 current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256 is resolved by not using that editorial snapshot as a predicate: this is a NO order, and the lead is cited only as an the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10222 at 16 FR 2247, in the Federal Register of March 13, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, is signed March 8, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Mar. 12, 1951. Text and inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses. Paragraph 1 transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration so much of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board as relates to civil defense, to remain under the jurisdiction of the Federal Civil Defense Administrator \"until further order of the President.\" Paragraph 2 transfers the related property and records of the Board, and the personnel of the Health Resources Office engaged primarily in those functions, as the Board's Chairman and the Administrator jointly determine. Paragraph 3 reads \"This order shall be effective as of March 4, 1951.\" Ending: Executive Order 12919, National Defense Industrial Resources Preparedness, signed June 3, 1994 and printed at 59 FR 29525 in the Federal Register of June 7, 1994 (held govinfo text layer), provides in section 904(a) that \"The following are superseded or revoked:\" and lists as item (2) \"Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247)\". Neither section 904 nor any other part of that order states an effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of June 7, 1994 is not used. The machine U.S. Code search found the editorial note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 that records the same revocation by section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919. Unnamed earlier candidates, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments: the editorial note printed with this order in the held OFR 1989 Codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_10222.txt) says that Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration, effective July 1, 1958, and consolidated its functions into the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization, and that Executive Order 10952 of July 20, 1961 later transferred civil defense functions to the Secretary of Defense. The text of the reorganization plan is not held; the held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10952 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10952.txt, 26 FR 6577) does not name this order. Neither instrument names Executive Order 10222, and no held source shows that either extinguished its commands; the same 1989 Codification still printed the order as in force on January 20, 1989. Neither has an evidence record in this dossier, so each is disclosed here rather than recorded as a later event. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12919 supersession or revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the held texts of Executive Order 12919 and in the OFR 1989 Codification.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958, which terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration, and Executive Order 10952 of July 20, 1961, which moved civil defense functions to the Secretary of Defense, are known here from the editorial note in the held OFR 1989 Codification; neither names Executive Order 10222, and no held source shows the order's commands extinguished by them. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments they are disclosed earlier candidates, not ends. (2) The words until further order of the President in paragraph 1 make the jurisdiction command contingent; the only held presidential order that names this order and ends it is Executive Order 12919. (3) The transfers in paragraph 2 were one-time acts, but no held source dates their completion, so no exhaustion date is asserted. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Paragraph 1 (jurisdiction over the transferred functions until further order of the President) and paragraph 2 (the transfer of property, records and personnel) are distinct commands of the same order, and paragraph 3 fixes the order's effective date. None has its own source, statute or earlier end shown in held evidence; each shares the supersession by Executive Order 12919, and the executed transfers survive as accrued effects.\",\"savings_check\":\"The executed transfers are accrued effects (state transferred_or_accrued). The source is the saving language of section 903 of Executive Order 12919, which keeps prior actions in effect unless inconsistent with that order and preserves the validity of anything done under previous delegations.\",\"scope_check\":\"Section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 names Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247) without exception or limitation, so it reaches all three clauses. The dossier note that the 1989 current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256 does not affect this claim: the order is a NO order, the 1989 Codification is not used as a current predicate, and it is cited only for its editorial observations, which predate the 1994 supersession.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[{"file_sha256":"9fea503fcb6a0a237442acdd1a35cec14b467e7bcf22422f2e5da8fa80c3b76f","path":"research/excavator/claude-erasmus-2026-11-02/r2/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-erasmus-2026-11-02/r2/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW.jsonl","pointer":"line:5","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"9fea503fcb6a0a237442acdd1a35cec14b467e7bcf22422f2e5da8fa80c3b76f","path":"research/excavator/claude-erasmus-2026-11-02/r2/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW.jsonl","pointer":"line:5","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"}],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:10222#1"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:10222#1"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:10222#2"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:10222#2"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:10222#3"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:10222#3"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"4136b7810d42ba86087ec48ac0b2edda3f8b313cce625fbab92b62ddbf5c16e6","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12919.txt","sha256":"4136b7810d42ba86087ec48ac0b2edda3f8b313cce625fbab92b62ddbf5c16e6","state":"match"},"sha256":"1035fc173d4e4d71bc4e2e140fa037e8c59be84185b6eba09b7f522198d79bbc","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12919.txt","text_sha256":"4136b7810d42ba86087ec48ac0b2edda3f8b313cce625fbab92b62ddbf5c16e6"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"5e744fa498f9cde39f8a2e9b0a14f3e330d8dceee4642fa008d63bf3a5ee9aad","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10222.txt","sha256":"5e744fa498f9cde39f8a2e9b0a14f3e330d8dceee4642fa008d63bf3a5ee9aad","state":"match"},"sha256":"580a64b4658ec58cae0e9ea5709b5689dfa01a3c41b3ba168f0a56417d55a169","text_path":"jobs/fr-origina \nmore years of such service under either \npermanent or indefinite appointment: \nProvided, That any such employees who \nleft their positions prior to the effective \ndate of this order to enter the armed \nforces of the United States and are re­\nemployed in the competitive service after \nthe effective date of this order pursuant \nto application for employment made \nwithin ninety days after honorable dis­\ncharge, or after hospitalization continu­\ning after discharge for not more than \none year, shall have their former indef­\ninite appointments converted to career- \nconditional or career appointments in \naccordance with this section:."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10440>EO:10577@5807ae84062cb63a","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no - **ACT:EO:10440>EO:10577@8e341773bcb178a7**; S1a576c2450e19e293e3536c9; {"actor_id":"EO:10577","char_end":32536,"char_start":31742,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":19100,"char_start":18987,"text":"Such exceptions from the competitive service shall be effective upon publication thereof in the FEDERAL REGISTER."},{"char_end":22167,"char_start":22082,"text":"Such changes shall become effective upon publication thereof in the FEDERAL REGISTER."},{"char_end":25615,"char_start":24195,"text":"(a) Under such conditions as the Civil Service Commission may prescribe, all employees serving under indefinite appointments in the competitive service on the effective date of this order who were appointed by selection in regular order from appropriate competitive civil-service registers established subsequent to February 4, 1946, shall, as of the effective date of this order, have their appointments converted to career-conditional appointments if they have had less than three years of creditable service, and to career appointments if they have had three or more years of such service since they were appointed: Provided, That any such employees who left their positions prior to the effective date of this order to enter the armed forces of the United States and are reemployed in the competitive service after the effective date of this order pursuant to application for employment made within ninety days after honorable discharge, or after hospitalization continuing after discharge for not more than one year, shall have their former indefinite appointments converted to career-conditional or career appointments in accordance with this section: Provided further, That employees serving in excepted positions who would meet the conditions for career-conditional or career appointments if they were serving in competitive positions shall be granted competitive status upon completion of a probationary period."},{"char_end":25987,"char_start":25617,"text":"(b) The Commission may prescribe the conditions under which employees who are serving under indefinite appointments in the competitive service on the effective date of this order and who were not appointed by selection in regular order from competitive civil-service registers may be examined and have their names entered on existing competitive civil-service registers."},{"char_end":27816,"char_start":26313,"text":"(c) All employees in the competitive service who on the effective date of this order are serving under indefinite appointments made noncompetitively based upon prior service with a competitive status shall, as of the effective date of this order, have their appointments converted to career-conditional appointments if they have had less than three years of creditable service, and to career appointments if they have had three or more years of such service under either permanent or indefinite appointment: Provided, That any such employees who left their positions prior to the effective date of this order to enter the armed forces of the United States and are reemployed in the competitive service after the effective date of this order pursuant to application for employment made within ninety days after honorable discharge, or after hospitalization continuing after discharge for not more than one year, shall have their former indefinite appointments converted to career-conditional or career appointments in accordance with this section: Provided further, That any such employees in the field service of the Post Office Department whose salary rates are fixed by the act of July 6, 1945, 59 Stat. 435, as heretofore or hereafter amended and supplemented, shall have their appointments converted to career appointments if they are serving in positions in the authorized complement of permanent positions (consisting of regular positions and positions within the authorized quota of substitutes)."},{"char_end":32645,"char_start":32546,"text":"This order shall become effective on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after the date hereof."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10440>EO:10577@8e341773bcb178a7","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. 10577)."],"research_rationale":"EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Federal Register Document 53-3883, filed 1953-04-30) orders that, until June 30, 1953, specified federal tax returns for periods through 1952 are open to inspection by the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives or a duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with the inquiry authorized by its resolution of January 27, 1953 into the administration of the Department of Justice and the Office of the Attorney General, subject to the conditions in the Treasury decision approved the same date. The held Federal Register text file contains this order followed by unrelated Civil Service Commission rules and a contents page from the same issue; the dossier's eleven clauses (including scopes labelled Schedule C, items and 633) were generated from those neighbouring documents, so the inventory is corrected to the single operative paragraph of the order. The order is a time-limited permission whose own wording fixes its end, so the terminating event is the stated until-date. Per the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates the end is recorded inclusive as 1953-06-30 (the order runs through that day); the alternative exclusive reading is that it ends when that day begins. No extension, amendment, revocation or supersession was found: the selected machine searches report none, and a search of all held order texts for the number 10451 and for inspection orders for this Committee finds only this order itself and orders for other committees or other periods.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No earlier end was found. The selected searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) report no instrument acting on this order, and a regular-expression search of the held order texts for its number found no order other than itself. The permission is tied to an inquiry, but nothing held shows that the inquiry or the Committee's use of the permission ended before June 30, 1953, and a deadline or condition is not treated as proof that an event occurred.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"There is no independent command. The order contains one permission (inspection of the listed returns by the Committee) limited by the same sentence to the period ending June 30, 1953, and by the conditions of the Treasury decision it refers to. No delegation, reporting duty or standing rule is present.\",\"savings_check\":\"The order has no savings sentence. Inspections made while the permission ran were completed acts, and nothing in the order or in any held later instrument continues, revives or extends the permission after its end. The Treasury decision it incorporates is not an instrument held in this packet, and this claim makes no finding about it.\",\"scope_check\":\"The dossier clauses other than the lead were produced from the Civil Service Commission Schedule C rules and the issue contents printed after the order on the same page, so they are not clauses of this order. The corrected inventory is one clause covering the single operative paragraph of the order, from the words beginning By virtue of the authority to the words ending approved by me this date (characters 772 to 1755 of the held text), which contains every operative word of the order.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:10451#corrected-1"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:10451#corrected-1"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"ccedef0eb4af86624039b55b3b655411aaa0bcd7e17e4183d21db1b127323ef1","path":"jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10451.txt","sha256":"ccedef0eb4af86624039b55b3b655411aaa0bcd7e17e4183d21db1b127323ef1","state":"match"},"sha256":"5ec04e21c5987e47704452407c16f599200940d3157ae22d26f4bc8651ea0cbd","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10451.txt","text_sha256":"ccedef0eb4af86624039b55b3b655411aaa0bcd7e17e4183d21db1b127323ef1"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"ccedef0eb4af86624039b55b3b655411aaa0bcd7e17e4183d21db1b127323ef1","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10451.txt","sha256":"ccedef0eb4af86624039b55b3b655411aaa0bcd7e17e4183d21db1b127323ef1","state":"match"},"sha256":"5ec04e21c5987e47704452407c16f599200940d3157ae22d26f4bc8651ea0cbd","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10451.txt","text_sha256":"ccedef0eb4af86624039b55b3b655411aaa0bcd7e17e4183d21db1b127323ef1"}]}]}

the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11195 (30 FR 1169, Federal Register of February 4, 1965), signed by Lyndon B. Johnson and dated January 30, 1965; number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's seven clauses (two amendment leads, four added positions and the effective-date sentence) cover every sentence of the order; I confirm them. Under section 303(g) of the Government Employees Salary Reform Act of 1964 the order amends Executive Order 11189 of November 23, 1964 by adding to its section 1 the Chief of Protocol, Department of State, as a Level IV position and to its section 2 three Level V positions (Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights; Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis, and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity; General Counsel, Veterans Administration), and takes effect immediately. Ending: Executive Order 12060 (signed 1978-05-15) revokes this order by number in its section 3, and EO 11189 by the same sentence. The first end of every clause is that express revocation; amendments continue until the amended order ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments). Earlier candidate end that does not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; it is not the end because it does not name EO 11195): Pub. L. 89-554 (Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 378), which enacted title 5 of the United States Code, lists in 5 U.S.C. 5315 \"(73) Chief of Protocol, Department of State.\" and in 5 U.S.C. 5316 item (101), the Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity, \"(110) General Counsel of the Veterans' Administration.\" and \"(114) Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights.\", so every position this order added appears in the statute (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11195_Pub._L._89-554_Sept._6_1966_80_Stat._378_et_seq._including_5_U.S.C._5315_and_5316_as__c629b8a1e7.txt; it is not an evidence record of this dossier, so it is pinned here by path). The Federal Register catalog note on EO 11189 says that order was \"Nullified by 80 Stat. 460, 461 (5 U.S.C. 5315, 5316)\" because the statute included all positions added by EO 11189 and its amendment EO 11195 (jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv), but the catalog note on EO 11195 itself records only the EO 12060 revocation. Section 7(c) of the same Act provides that an order in effect under a replaced law continues in effect under the corresponding provision \"until repealed, amended, or superseded.\", which points the other way. I did not establish that the statute extinguished this order, so EO 12060 is recorded as the first end. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, whose hits for this order are the historical notes under 5 U.S.C. 5315 and 5316 and the 5 U.S.C. 5317 note stating that the order was revoked by Ex. Ord. The dossier's seven clauses (two amendment leads, four added positions and the effective-date sentence) cover every sentence of the order, so I confirm the inventory. EO 12060 (signed 1978-05-15) revokes the order by number in its section 3, and the dossier carries the ACT record for it. The first end of every clause is that express revocation. Amendments continue until the amended order ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, and EO 11189 was revoked by the same sentence. Earlier candidate end that does not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; it is not the end because it does not name EO 11195): Pub. L. 89-554 (Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 378), which enacted title 5 of the United States Code, lists in 5 U.S.C. 5315 the Chief of Protocol, Department of State, as item (73), and in 5 U.S.C. 5316 the Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity as item (101), the General Counsel of the Veterans' Administration as item (110) and the Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights as item (114), so every position this order added appears in the statute (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11195_Pub._L._89-554_Sept._6_1966_80_Stat._378_et_seq._including_5_U.S.C._5315_and_5316_as__c629b8a1e7.txt). Section 7(c) of the same Act says an order in effect under a replaced law continues in effect under the corresponding provision \"until repealed, amended, or superseded\", which points the other way. I did not establish that the statute extinguished this order, so EO 12060 is recorded as the first end. The 5 U.S.C. 5317 note in the U.S. Code release point also records that this order was revoked by EO 12060. days after the final report). The clause ended on that date or, at the latest, on 1968-04-29 (EO 11409 item 1(b)). Needs the commission's report and termination record."],"research_rationale":"EO 11262 adds three items to EO 11248: in level IV, (4) Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice; in level V, (4) Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and (5) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Legislative Affairs). No later amender deleted the two level V items (traced item by item through EO 11699); they ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11409 item 1(b) formally deleted the level IV item on April 29, 1968. That position, however, belonged to a temporary commission: EO 11236 (held, 30 FR 9349) required the commission to report within 18 months and to terminate not later than 90 days after its report. The placement therefore probably lost its object before the 1968 deletion. Deadlines cannot fix the actual date, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is unaffected because the two level V items ran to 1973-03-23. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:11262#sec1-item4-level-IV"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:11262#sec2-item4-level-V"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:11262#sec2-item5-level-V"}],"source_pins":[]}]}

Needs the 1970 statute and the text of Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1970 to decide whether the Interior commissioner position was abolished or continued under the EO 11587 title."],"research_rationale":"EO 11293 adds a single item (8), Commissioner, Federal Water Pollution Control Administration, Department of the Interior, to level V of EO 11248. The family trace shows two later events on that item before the 1973 revocation. EO 11587 (March 15, 1971) substitutes the words 'Commissioner, Water Quality Office, Environmental Protection Agency' for the original description, and EO 11604 (July 2, 1971) deletes item (8). Retitling the item as an office of a different agency shows that the administration had been renamed and transferred before March 1971. Held sources cannot settle whether that statutory reorganization abolished the Interior position, which would end this placement earlier, or carried it forward under the new title, so that the placement ran to the July 2, 1971 deletion. The OFR 'Revoked by EO 11708' disposition is only a formal later event; the whole-order end is left open. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. If it was abolished then, the clause ceased earlier than the formal deletion; first_end and whole_order_end are left open."],"research_rationale":"EO 11299 of August 15, 1966 (official text 31 FR 10917, saved OCR text layer read in full; the order fills PDF page 7, pages 8-9 are blank and regulations) adds '(9) Director, Urban Transportation Administration, Department of Housing and Urban Development' to section 2 (level V) of EO 11248. The 1989 OFR disposition table records it as superseded by EO 11708 (March 23, 1973), whose section 3 revokes EO 11248 as amended except for eight listed level V positions, none of them this one. But the saved-text corpus shows an earlier event: EO 11634 of December 6, 1971 (36 FR 23287, read in full) paragraph 2(a) deletes the item, then numbered (8). And the office itself may have ceased with the 1968 transfer of urban mass transportation functions to the Department of Transportation, which no held source settles. The clause is terminated by 1971-12-06 at the latest, but its first end is not asserted. Whether the 1970 substitution ended this placement (a different, generic OMB office) or only retitled the same position, so that the clause ended in 1973, is a legal judgment no held source settles; first_end and whole_order_end are left open, with both events recorded as later events."],"research_rationale":"EO 11367 of August 18, 1967 (official text 32 FR 12037, saved OCR text layer read in full; the order fills PDF page 7) adds '(5) Assistant Director for Executive Management, Bureau of the Budget, Executive Office of the President' to section 1 (level IV) of EO 11248. The 1989 OFR disposition table records it as superseded by EO 11708 of March 23, 1973 (38 FR 7979, read in full), whose section 3 revokes EO 11248 as amended except for eight level V positions. The saved-text corpus shows an earlier event: EO 11540 of July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10735, read in full) substitutes 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget' for this order's words, effective July 1, 1970. The clause is terminated by 1973 at the latest, but which event first ended it is not asserted (see gap). Partial claim.","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:11367#adds-assistant-director-executive-management-bob-level-iv"}],"source_pins":[]},{"claim_sha256":"9e37c85aa2ffbef9ceed0d4a0694a9c1ada803bcc92f3cae5674baf31e3fbf81","current_canonical":false,"locations":[{"file_sha256":"b2636f560ec738104c3115a11c7abbd3e2fba970dc2b24d85c58e085e2de5912","path":"research/excavator/craigellachie-ii-2026-10-20/01/applied-v1/CLAIMS.proposed.jsonl","pointer":"line:1"}],"reported_material_gaps":[],"research_rationale":"EO 11367 (signed 1967-08-18, 32 FR 12037; held official Federal Register text read in full) adds item (5), 'Assistant Director for Executive Management, Bureau of the Budget, Executive Office of the President', to section 1 (level IV) of EO 11248. It has one operative sentence, a standing pay-level designation under 5 U.S.C. 5317, with no term or condition. The rest of the held extract (migratory-bird and other regulations on the same pages) is neighbouring material, not part of the order. Newly held: Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1970 (84 Stat. 2085-2086, read in full). Sec. 102(a) provides 'The Bureau of the Budget in the Executive Office of the President is hereby designated as the Office of Management and Budget'; sec. 102(b) designates the statutory Assistant Directors (31 U.S.C. 16a, 16c) Assistant Directors of OMB; sec. 103 makes the Bureau's records, property and personnel OMB's. That is a redesignation of the same entity and offices, so it abolishes nothing and is not an end. The Statutes at Large marginal note gives 'Effective July 1, 1970' for the plan, and sec. 301 sets July 1, 1970 as the floor; no end date in this claim depends on that note. EO 11540 (signed 1970-07-01, 35 FR 10735; held, read in full) states 'This order shall be effective July 1, 1970' and substitutes, in item (5), 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President' for the words of this order. I treat that as a conforming retitle, recorded as a later event and not as the first end: the item keeps its number and level IV, and the substituted title covers every OMB Assistant Director, including any post that was the former Assistant Director for Executive Management, so the placement was widened and renamed, not withdrawn. The dossier has no OMB organization record (the request was answered with the plan only); the judgment does not need one because the retitled item has a live object under sec. 102(b). The first end is EO 11708 (signed 1973-03-23, 38 FR 7979; held, read in full), sec. 3: 'Except with respect to the positions enumerated in section 2 of this order, Executive Order No. 11248 of October 10, 1965, as amended, is hereby revoked.' EO 11708 states no effective date or delay, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1973-03-23. Sec. 2 continues only eight level V positions, none of them OMB, so item (5) (level IV) is revoked; sec. 1(9) of EO 11708 places 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget' in level IV under its own authority, a new placement and not a residue of this order. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR disposition catalog: hits read, all EO 11540/11708) carry no coverage warning. A reviewer should test (a) whether EO 11540's substitution should be the first end instead (1970-07-01), and (b) whether the revocation date 1973-03-23 is right given EO 11708 has no effective-date wording.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Tested every instrument that could have ended or altered item (5) before 1973-03-23. (a) Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1970 (held, read in full): sec. 102(a) designates the Bureau of the Budget itself as OMB, sec. 102(b) redesignates the statutory Assistant Director offices, sec. 103 transfers its personnel to OMB; nothing is abolished, so no statutory end. (b) EO 11540 (held, effective July 1, 1970 by its own sentence): retitles item (5); treated as a later event, not an end, for the coverage reason given in the rationale. (c) I read the operative paragraphs of every other amender of EO 11248 issued after 1967-08-18 (EO 11369, 11384, 11385, 11389, 11393, 11400, 11409, 11416, 11421, 11441, 11463, 11468, 11489, 11499, 11504, 11510, 11516, 11542, 11550, 11581, 11587, 11604, 11634, 11641, 11676, 11699). None deletes, replaces or renumbers section 1 item (5): EO 11385 added item (6); EO 11389 added item (7); EO 11581 deleted item (6) and renumbered (7)-(11), leaving (5); EO 11409, 11441, 11468, 11489, 11604, 11634, 11641, 11676 and 11699 touch other section 1 items; the rest concern section 2 (level V). (d) No own-term, sunset or self-termination: the order is a single placement. (e) The OFR disposition catalog hits and the 1989 table point only to EO 11540 and EO 11708. The first end found is EO 11708 sec. 3.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order contains one operative sentence, an amendment adding item (5) to EO 11248 sec. 1. The only continuing effect is the level IV designation under 5 U.S.C. 5317. It imposes no duty on any officer, no report, no fixed term and no condition, and it is a standing designation, not a performed command, so it lasted until altered or revoked. No independent command survives the revocation.\",\"savings_check\":\"Searched EO 11708 secs. 1-3 and EO 11540 for saving wording as stated in the savings reason: none for item (5). Transferred or accrued effects: none; the level IV placement of the OMB Assistant Director is re-made by EO 11708 sec. 1(9) under that order's own authority, which is that order's provision, not a residue of EO 11367.\",\"scope_check\":\"The first end is the revocation of the parent order EO 11248 as amended; the machine record marks scope 'partial' because of the exception for the sec. 2 positions. I read sec. 2 of EO 11708: it continues eight level V positions (Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (Comptroller); Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Reserve Affairs; Assistant Secretary, Comptroller, HEW; Deputy Commissioner of Social Security; Commissioner on Aging; Deputy Director, Secret Service; Commissioner, Property Management and Disposal Service, GSA; Deputy Assistant Secretary for Model Cities, HUD). None is item (5), and item (5) is a section 1 (level IV) item while sec. 2 continues only level V positions, so the revocation reaches this clause in full. The whole order is this one item, so the whole-order end is the clause end.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:11367#whole"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"c26ca16e827d33864a9448e0e1eecbcf4239c4a64916f841478d9ac1dc71b9d8","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11708.txt","sha256":"c26ca16e827d33864a9448e0e1eecbcf4239c4a64916f841478d9ac1dc71b9d8","state":"match"},"sha256":"cc47994b2f4054913b76f251ac8970a70190e7ac65586ed1c1637422c87d8f92","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11708.txt","text_sha256":"c26ca16e827d33864a9448e0e1eecbcf4239c4a64916f841478d9ac1dc71b9d8"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"256ec8fe083e88e7f8e341a2b08300f80718e3170ec221b791304bc7359f87ee","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11540.txt","sha256":"256ec8fe083e88e7f8e341a2b08300f80718e3170ec221b791304bc7359f87ee","state":"match"},"sha256":"0019cc2ee91535188b4ee6744f7515940bf7ad1951f742b967d552735fd54398","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11540.txt","text_sha256":"256ec8fe083e88e7f8e341a2b08300f80718e3170ec221b791304bc7359f87ee"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"ae7e88390b21b55cbb4c8f7dcec10cd9de94b3c56f435d5a6973f65400bc8928","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11367.txt","sha256":"ae7e88390b21b55cbb4c8f7dcec10cd9de94b3c56f435d5a6973f65400bc8928","state":"match"},"sha256":"ccbf1988d46a36bebbf372fa34f4250ad98761eef57096cc25f232db35306120","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11367.txt","text_sha256":"ae7e88390b21b55cbb4c8f7dcec10cd9de94b3c56f435d5a6973f65400bc8928"}]}]}

In level IV of EO 11248 it (1a) replaces item (3), the Food-for-Peace Special Assistant, with the Administrator, SRS; (1b) replaces item (4), the crime commission's Executive Secretary, with the Administrator, NIH; and (1c) adds (8) the Administrator, HSMHA and (9) the Executive Director, Cabinet Committee on Price Stability. In level V it (2) replaces item (15), the Administrator, SRS, with the Deputy Administrator, HSMHA. Items (3), (4), (8) and (15) survived every later amender and ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11708 sec. 1 places the first three positions anew by its own authority; none is a sec. 2 exception. EO 11468 formally deleted item (9) on May 10, 1969. The committee was an ad hoc body, and no held source shows when it was discontinued, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is 1973-03-23 in any case. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.","rationale":"I read the complete held EO 11417 (33 FR 10625, July 24, 1968; the held extract also carries unrelated neighbouring rules): one sentence amending sec. 305 of EO 10973 of Nov. 3, 1961, 'as amended', by adding the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business to the Development Loan Committee; no own term and no savings clause, and its operative effect exists only as text of EO 10973. I read the held full text of EO 12163 (44 FR 56673, Sept. 29, 1979) including secs. 1-902 to 1-905: sec. 1-903(a)(1) provides 'The following are revoked: (1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3, 1961, as amended', which removes the base order, with all its amendments (EO 11417 among them), from force, and sec. 1-905 makes it effective October 1, 1979. EO 11417 is not individually named in EO 12163, and the machine-selected ACT: spans for EO 12163 are wrong passages (allocation and references provisions) so I do not cite them; the basis is my reading of the actor text. Sec. 1-904 saves earlier delegations, determinations, regulations and similar actions 'made, issued, or entered into with respect to any function affected by this order' until amended or terminated; I read that as preserving executed administrative actions under the foreign-assistance functions, not the Development Loan Committee membership amendment, which is a rule of the revoked order's text, but this is a judgment recorded as a residual risk. The catalog note ('Revoked by: EO 12163, September 29, 1979') and 1989 row ('Revoked by EO 12163') agree but are leads only. Other machine-found chain orders (EO 11579, 11685, 11816, 11959, 12118) amend or supersede parts of EO 10973 and cannot end EO 11417 on their own. The held text layer also carries neighbouring Commerce regulations on the same pages, which are not part of the order. End: the parent was revoked by Executive Order 12163, effective October 1, 1979, Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) states in section 1-903(a) that the following are revoked: \"(1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;\" and in section 1-905 \"The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979.\" Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. Needs the statute's commencement provisions and the Postal Service commencement date."],"research_rationale":"EO 11468 (1) replaces level IV item (9), the Executive Director of the Cabinet Committee on Price Stability, with the Deputy Under Secretary for International Labor Affairs, and (2) adds level V items (23) Deputy Assistant Postmaster General, Bureau of Operations and (24) Director, Office of Minority Business Enterprise. Item (9) was renumbered (8) by EO 11581 and ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973; EO 11708 sec. 1(12) places the same position anew. Item (24) was replaced by EO 11516 on March 19, 1970. Item (23) was renumbered and then formally deleted by EO 11634 on December 6, 1971. Before that, however, the Postal Reorganization Act (Pub. L. 91-375) abolished the Post Office Department, whose positions the 5 U.S.C. 5315 notes show it struck. That earlier statutory end is probable but not dated in held sources, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is 1973-03-23 in any case. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Removing the old item was completed on December 11, 1969. EO 11708 does not continue or re-place it. EO 11768 (February 20, 1974) lists a Commissioner, Automated Data and Telecommunications Service, GSA, which shows that GSA reorganized the service at some date. If that reorganization came before March 23, 1973 and abolished the Transportation and Communications Service commissioner, this placement ended earlier. The date is not in held sources, so the first end is left open. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The order establishes the Missouri River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3: a Chairman, Federal agency members, State members and interstate agency members), its functions (Section 4) and international coordination (Section 5) and reporting (Section 6) sections. Its held text has no sunset or termination provision.  First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.  Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 4 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (4 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (5 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11882, EO 12038, EO 12148, EO 12319.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11882, EO 12038, EO 12148, EO 12319. The orders amending this one (EO 11882, EO 12038, EO 12148) change membership or jurisdiction and end nothing. Own terms: the held text has no sunset, fixed term or termination condition. EO 12319 Section 1 (commissions listed as terminated in 1981) names commissions, not this order, and is disclosed as an earlier candidate; the order itself was revoked by Section 5.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"All commands of this order concern the Commission's existence, membership, functions and reporting; none is a one-time command, so none was spent before the Commission's order was revoked.\",\"savings_check\":\"I read the full held Federal Register text of EO 12319 (46 FR 45591). Its Sections 2 to 4 direct agencies to cooperate in an orderly close-out, transfer commission assets to the member States subject to the approval of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, and direct Federal agency members to continue coordination; none of them preserves the revoked order or any command of it, so I find no saving clause. The asset transfer is a one-time transition arrangement of the commissions, not a command of this order.\",\"scope_check\":\"The revocation names the order as amended by number. The order establishes the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3), functions (Section 4), consultation with adjoining States (Section 5) and reporting (Section 6). Its held text has no sunset or termination provision. EO 11737 (1973) rewrote Sections 2 and 5, changed the State list in Section 3(3) and inserted a new international-coordination section, redesignating Section 6 as Section 7. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.
